tickets.title: Contracts generate typed models and enforce the dual-path bid boundary
tickets.objective: packages/contracts: JSON Schemas per DESIGN §Interfaces (partner-reconciled Intent with hard_constraints/preferences, Bid with optional message + seller_asserted provenance, VerificationResult), codegen to Pydantic + TS, and boundary validation: hosted bids reject on any non-hook provenance; external bids admit seller_asserted claims flagged for verification; expired/blacklisted/invalid reject on every path. OpenAPI examples + consumer contract tests for every cross-domain endpoint. Also owns the shared policy contract D13 places in this package: the versioned RankingWeights object the single published rank formula reads its weights, normalization bounds and penalty caps from. The SellerEligibility port is NOT here: amendment 1 (D54) places it in apps/exchange/src/eligibility, owned by T-030, because that is where the amended frozen suite imports it from. Amendment 1 adds two more contracts to this package. (a) The external SigningEnvelope: signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce and schema_version are REQUIRED on every Bid submitted through POST /v1/auctions/{auction_id}/bids, plus the single canonical-signing-bytes function over (auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version, payload_hash) that both signer and verifier call. No optional-field or legacy-tolerant variant exists on the production contract. (b) TrustSnapshot.dims is SIX dimensions - price_honored, discount_honored, shipped_on_time, not_returned, feedback_match, catalog_claim_accuracy - inside one trust system, per D53.
acceptance: 1. Schema→codegen produces importable py+ts types for all pinned objects incl. VerificationResult
2. Hosted-path bid with a seller_asserted claim rejects; external-path bid with the same claim admits flagged-for-verification; expired/blacklisted reject on both
3. Round-trip serialization passes in both languages; every cross-domain endpoint has a checked-in OpenAPI example + contract test

4. RankingWeights is a generated, versioned contract type importable in py+ts, carrying the five published weights, the normalization bounds and the penalty catalogue, and a weight set that does not sum to 1.0 is invalid

5. SigningEnvelope (D52): a Bid missing any one of signer_id/key_id/issued_at/nonce/schema_version fails schema validation in py+ts, and a Bid carrying all five validates - so a schema that rejects everything cannot satisfy this

6. TrustSnapshot carries exactly six dims incl. catalog_claim_accuracy (D53): a six-dim snapshot round-trips in py+ts, a snapshot omitting catalog_claim_accuracy is invalid, and a snapshot naming a seventh dimension is invalid.
tickets.verify: pytest packages/contracts -q && npx vitest run packages/contracts
non_goals: No service code; schema changes after this land only via E1 tickets

Amendment 1 (D52) adds two app.* structures: app.seller_endpoints holds one row per live key (signer_id, store_id, key_id, public_key, status) so a signer's keys can rotate and key_id is unique only within a signer, and app.bid_nonces (signer_id, nonce, auction_id, consumed_at, retain_until) is the durable store behind the NonceStore port, UNIQUE on (signer_id, nonce), retained past the auction's respond_by.

2. Grant test: exchange role SELECT on sealed.* fails
3. commerce_events enforces idempotency_key uniqueness and valid prev_hash; replay reproduces stream hash

4. Replay store (D52): app.bid_nonces rejects a duplicate (signer_id, nonce) via the uniqueness constraint while accepting the same nonce string under a different signer_id, and app.seller_endpoints holds two live rows for one signer_id under different key_id values plus a row where a DIFFERENT signer_id reuses one of those key_id strings - so a schema keyed on key_id alone, or one key per store, fails this criterion

tickets.title: Auctions fan out, time out, and always represent every store
tickets.objective: Auction state machine in Redis; POST /auctions; parallel BidRequest fan-out with hard timeout; list-price fallback bids for Tier-0 and non-responding stores (R10). Also creates apps/exchange/src/eligibility (the versioned SellerEligibility port: base class with interface_version and check(store_id) -> EligibilityDecision{store_id, status, reason}, the statuses ELIGIBLE/BLACKLISTED/UNAVAILABLE, and SELLER_ELIGIBILITY_INTERFACE_VERSION) and the apps/exchange/src/orchestration package with the R12 solicitation gate solicit_bids(roster=, solicitor=, eligibility=, now=) -> {solicited, entries, denied}. solicit_bids reads eligibility for every rostered store before any store is asked. The gate sits above collect_bids — collect_bids keeps its (roster, responses, now) parameters and is handed an already-eligible roster.
acceptance: 1. Auction with 3 responsive + 1 silent + 2 Tier-0 stores yields 6 ranked entries, silent one at list price
2. Timeout enforced (frozen clock); late bids rejected
3. State machine transitions logged to ledger via trust API stub

4. Solicitation gate (R12/D54, fail-closed, at the public orchestration boundary, by DENIAL): solicit_bids consults SellerEligibility for every rostered store before fan-out. A BLACKLISTED store, an UNAVAILABLE store and a store whose eligibility read RAISES are each never handed to the solicitor and never appear even as a list-price fallback entry, and each is recorded in the result's denied list with a reason naming its condition. Positive control in the same test: eligible stores ARE solicited in roster order, appear as non-fallback entries, and their solicited prices survive the orchestration layer - so an orchestration that solicits nobody fails here. collect_bids keeps its (roster, responses, now) parameters unchanged and never receives an eligibility argument
non_goals: No accept_offer - T-033 adds it to the same orchestration package and must not modify solicit_bids; the two never run concurrently (T-033 depends on T-030)

tickets.title: Shortlists rank by the single published formula behind eligibility filters
tickets.objective: Eligibility filters (blacklist fail-closed, offer expiry, checkout-domain validity, hard constraints requiring verified facts per R19), then published rank_score per DESIGN §Decisions with [0,1]-normalized features, policy penalties, stable tie-breaking, component map + human-readable explanation; slotting ≤4 with graceful collapse; provenance + verification-warning labels. The eligibility filter is the R12 ranking gate (D54): rank() consults SellerEligibility and excludes the ineligible candidate with a recorded exclusion reason, fail-closed on an unavailable read. Trust inputs are the six-dimension TrustSnapshot (D53); ranking reads the snapshot's score/confidence and never re-derives dimensions.
acceptance: 1. Golden tests: fixed inputs → exact eligibility set, ranking, slots, explanations
2. Blindness test: tier/fee fields cannot alter score; contradicted hard constraint never wins regardless of other components (release blocker test)
3. Filter tests: blacklisted/expired/bad-domain/hard-fail excluded with exclusion_reasons recorded; slots collapse at 1–3 stores

4. Ranking gate + versioned interface (R12/D54, fail-closed, by DENIAL with a positive control): a BLACKLISTED candidate is excluded before any score is computed with its exclusion_reasons entry recorded, an UNAVAILABLE read and a raising read each exclude rather than admit, and the same candidate with an ELIGIBLE verdict IS ranked and CAN win - so a ranker that excludes everything fails. SELLER_ELIGIBILITY_INTERFACE_VERSION is a non-empty string, the three statuses are distinct, and BOTH boundary gates (solicit_bids and accept_offer) refuse an eligibility source whose interface_version is not the published one while accepting one that is

tickets.title: Accepting an offer produces a validated code and permalink
tickets.objective: Accept endpoint resolves a CheckoutProvider (T-036) by CHECKOUT_MODE and delegates code creation to it, returns the permalink the provider mints, records the accepted event, and handles code-creation failure with re-offer of the next slot. The starting slice runs SimulatedRedirectProvider — the checkout URL is validated against the registered seller domain and checkout_redirect plus the downstream LedgerEvent kinds are emitted identically to the Shopify path (C11); Shopify mode selects the T-052 adapter behind the same port.
acceptance: 1. Accept → code+permalink via the resolved provider; ledger events emitted
2. Merchant failure path re-offers deterministically
3. Double-accept on one auction rejected
4. Redirect mode: off-domain checkout_url is refused (release blocker test); emitted event kinds match the Shopify-mode golden sequence

5. Checkout gate (R12/D54, fail-closed, at the public orchestration boundary, by DENIAL): accept_offer(auction=, bid_ref=, code_creator=, mode=, eligibility=) in apps/exchange/src/orchestration RE-READS eligibility at accept time, so a store blacklisted after it bid is refused - no code created (assert the code creator was never called), no permalink, and a denial_reason recorded; an UNAVAILABLE read and a read that RAISES each refuse identically. Positive control in the same test: an ELIGIBLE store with an available read is accepted, mints exactly one code, and returns an on-domain permalink containing that code. accept() keeps its four positional parameters (auction, bid_id, code_creator, mode) and gains no required parameter
non_goals: No edits to solicit_bids or apps/exchange/src/eligibility/** - T-030 owns both; this ticket only adds accept_offer to the orchestration package

tickets.title: Checkout reaches the merchant through a provider port
tickets.objective: apps/exchange/src/checkout: define CheckoutProvider — the single port every accept path goes through to turn a won offer into a discount code and a permalink — and ship SimulatedRedirectProvider as the required starting implementation, which needs no Shopify and no merchant app. Providers register under the CHECKOUT_MODE spellings accept() already resolves ('redirect' and the shopify_stub/shopify spellings); the port, not the provider, performs the registered-domain check, so no implementation can opt out of it, and every provider emits the identical ordered LedgerEvent kinds so nothing downstream can tell which one ran (C11). The Shopify path (T-052) is one adapter behind this port, not the route to a code.
acceptance: 1. CheckoutProvider is one port with a registered provider per CHECKOUT_MODE spelling; resolving an unregistered mode raises rather than silently falling back, and a lint/grep test asserts no code-minting call site exists outside a provider

2. SimulatedRedirectProvider mints a single-use code and an on-domain permalink with no Shopify dependency; the same fixture offer run through the Shopify adapter yields the identical ordered LedgerEvent kinds (C11 parity), so provider swap is invisible downstream

3. The port validates the offer's checkout_url host against the registered seller domain (bid['store_domain']) by exact match BEFORE any provider is asked to mint — rival domain, suffix spoof, glued-suffix spoof, userinfo spoof and subdomain are each refused with no code created (D22); an on-domain offer completes, so a surface that refuses everything cannot satisfy this criterion

4. Provider selection is the mode argument accept() already receives: accept(auction, bid_id, code_creator, mode) keeps its four positional parameters and its injected code creator, and registering a further provider adds no parameter to it
non_goals: No Shopify GraphQL calls — the Shopify adapter is T-052
No accept orchestration, no re-offer logic (T-033 owns those)

tickets.title: External bids enter signed with a required envelope and route to verification, not rejection
tickets.objective: Signature registration + verification on the external submission door POST /v1/auctions/{auction_id}/bids for non-hosted agents; schema validation admits seller_asserted claims and free-text message, marks the bid unverified, and enqueues extraction+verification carrying the submission's nonce as its idempotency key; hosted solicitation path (POST /v1/bid-requests) unchanged. Amendment 1 (D52) makes the signing envelope REQUIRED, not optional: signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce and schema_version are all mandatory and a submission missing any one is Rejected before enqueue. Public surface, all in packages/store_agent/src/external (the module does not move; the exchange route is its only public caller): sign_bid(payload, key); receive_bid(payload, signature, keyring, *, queue, nonce_store, now, auction_deadline, freshness_window_seconds); canonical_signing_bytes(payload) covering auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version and payload_hash(payload), order-independent and stable across a JSON round trip; NonceStore with seen(signer_id, nonce) and purge_expired(as_of). The keyring is {signer_id: {key_id: secret}} backed by app.seller_endpoints so keys rotate; an unknown (signer_id, key_id) pair rejects rather than falling back to another key of that signer, and a lookup keyed on key_id alone is wrong because two signers may reuse a key_id string.
acceptance: 1. Registered-key signed external bid carrying a complete envelope is accepted, marked unverified, and enqueued exactly once with the nonce as the queued item's idempotency key; a bad signature rejects and enqueues nothing. The positive case must pass, so a receiver that rejects everything fails this criterion
2. Hosted bid with non-hook provenance still rejects (regression)
3. Expired/blacklisted external bids reject before enqueue

4. Required envelope (D52): five submissions, each omitting exactly one of signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce, schema_version, are each rejected before enqueue; the otherwise-identical submission carrying all five is accepted

5. Canonical bytes and coverage (D52): canonical_signing_bytes is deterministic, independent of mapping insertion order and stable across a JSON round trip; payload_hash is a digest of at least 32 chars that changes when the offer body changes and appears inside the canonical bytes; mutating any of auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version or the offer body changes the bytes; and tampering with any of them after signing rejects at the door

6. Key rotation (D52): a signer with two live key_id rows verifies under either; a signature naming an unregistered key_id for a known signer rejects with no fallback to that signer's other key; and a second signer reusing the first signer's key_id string under a different secret does not verify - so a lookup keyed on key_id alone fails

7. Replay and freshness (D52): resubmitting an accepted payload rejects; a different nonce from the same signer is still accepted and the same nonce from a DIFFERENT signer is accepted (scoping is per signer); NonceStore.seen stays True after purge_expired at any moment before the auction deadline and becomes False only after it passes; a submission arriving after the auction deadline rejects; and an issued_at outside freshness_window_seconds rejects in both directions, far-past and clock-skewed-future

tickets.title: Trust merges verification and outcome observations against the approved manifest
tickets.objective: Merged observation framework over SIX dimensions (price_honored, discount_honored, shipped_on_time, not_returned, feedback_match, catalog_claim_accuracy) inside ONE trust system (D53): per-dimension Beta with observation-type weights (contradicted 2.0, severe policy 3.0, mismatch returns 1.5; verified claims + fulfilled purchases positive; capped conversion influence), time decay against recorded as-of time, neutral low-confidence prior ~Beta(2,2), score + confidence + score_version; published threshold; blacklist bound to business identity with review/appeal/expiry states and fail-closed reads. Each verification outcome routes to exactly one dimension through T-080's typed, exhaustive claim_type mapping - offer-integrity claim types to their transaction dimension, product-fact claim types to catalog_claim_accuracy - consumed read-only here.
acceptance: 1. Golden trajectories (verification-only, outcomes-only, mixed) match human-approved fixture manifest expectations
2. Decay + confidence property tests; conversion influence cap holds
3. Blacklist: identity-bound persistence, expiry/appeal states, and fail-closed read behavior (unavailable state blocks checkout) all tested

4. Bit-for-bit replay (R15, S3): recomputing every served TrustSnapshot from the genesis event stream reproduces score, confidence, score_version and each dimension's alpha, beta and decayed_at exactly, with decay evaluated against the recorded as-of time rather than wall clock — canonical serialization, event hash, sequence and stream identity all pinned

5. Six dimensions, one system (D53): a contradicted product-fact claim (ingredients / compatibility / nutrition / specifications) moves catalog_claim_accuracy and leaves feedback_match untouched, while a contradicted price claim moves price_honored and leaves catalog_claim_accuracy untouched; the served snapshot exposes all six dims and no seventh

6. Outcome treatment (D53): on the mapped dimension, verified moves the mean up; contradicted moves it down at weight 2.0; unsupported moves it down by the published fractional weight strictly less than contradicted's and its dominant effect is on confidence/coverage; ambiguous produces ZERO mean movement and lowers coverage/confidence only. Asserted as an ordering over four runs from one fixture state, so a no-op implementation fails

tickets.title: A golden pitch yields all four verification statuses with evidence
tickets.objective: packages/verification + trust-service wiring: atomic typed claim extraction with source spans (LLM behind strict schemas, doubles in tests), seller/SKU/variant resolution (ambiguous on failure), unit/type canonicalization, deterministic comparators per DESIGN, statuses verified|contradicted|unsupported|ambiguous with evidence refs + confidence, idempotent per (pitch, verifier version, catalog snapshot), re-verify only on snapshot/verifier change; results persist to ledger tables and emit trust_observations + claim_verified events. Every persisted VerificationResult claim carries the typed claim_type that T-080's exhaustive mapping routes to a trust dimension; an extracted claim whose claim_type is absent from the mapping raises rather than defaulting (D53).
acceptance: 1. Golden pitch fixture (true + false + unsupported + ambiguous claims) returns the four distinct statuses with evidence refs (S8, external ground truth: approved golden set)
2. Idempotency: re-running same (pitch, versions) writes nothing; snapshot bump re-verifies
3. Comparator unit tests: boolean/string normalization, numeric tolerance, price vs offer+catalog, set containment, relationship existence; injection strings in pitch text never execute (C10 test)

4. Typed routing (D53): each claim in the golden result carries a claim_type present in the manifest mapping, a product-fact claim_type routes to catalog_claim_accuracy and an offer-integrity claim_type routes to its transaction dimension, and an unmapped claim_type raises instead of silently defaulting
non_goals: No trust score math (T-062); no ranking
Does not author the golden set; fixtures/golden/** is T-080's human-approved ground truth, read-only here (closes the SPEC A3 circularity).

tickets.title: The approved manifest and seed generator define ground truth
tickets.objective: Fixture manifest: dishonest-store behaviors, new-store prior N, seeds, expected trust trajectories — submitted for human approval (approval artifact committed). Parameterized SEED_CATEGORY catalog generator + `make demo-seed` provisioning stub or live stores. Manifest also defines the golden intent/pitch set (incl. persona scripts, contradiction/stale/variant/unit/injection/claim-splitting cases) used by verification and eval gates.
acceptance: 1. Manifest + golden set committed with recorded human approval artifact
2. Generator seeds N stores incl. the dishonest one into shopify-stub from SEED_CATEGORY config
3. `make demo-seed` idempotent against stub

4. The manifest instantiates the published claim_type -> dimension mapping table (D53): every claim_type the golden set uses maps to exactly one of the SIX published trust dimensions, product-fact claim types (ingredients, compatibility, nutrition, specifications) map to catalog_claim_accuracy and offer-integrity claim types to their transaction dimension, the table states the treatment of verified/contradicted/unsupported/ambiguous outcomes, and loading a manifest containing an unmapped claim_type RAISES rather than defaulting. Every dishonest_store.behaviours[].dim value is one of the six. The table is an additional key alongside the existing manifest keys at fixtures/manifest.json

The manifest carries the mapping under the exact key `claim_type_dimensions` (that spelling is what the frozen tests read), and at least one `dishonest_store.behaviours[].dim` is `catalog_claim_accuracy`.

The golden set contains at least one product-fact claim with status `verified` AND at least one with status `contradicted` — a set that is all-true or all-false does not exercise the sixth trust dimension in both directions.

tickets.title: One scripted run proves the full S1 flow
tickets.objective: E2E test: intent→clarify→bids→shortlist→accept→code→stub checkout→pixel+webhook→reconcile→ledger→trust update, all against compose.
acceptance: 1. The full chain asserts an EXACT per-kind multiset over the complete LedgerEvent enum (D34), not "exactly once": bid_placed == n_stores_solicited (read from the run fixture); shown == len(shortlist.slots); auction_opened == auction_closed == accepted == code_created == checkout_redirect == checkout_pixel == order_paid == reconciled == 1; refund == order_fulfilled == feedback == offer_integrity == blacklisted == blacklist_expired == 0; claim_verified == the run's asserted-claim count. A subset or >=1 assertion does not satisfy this criterion.
2. Shortlist contained fallback + hosted bids
3. Run completes offline
4. Release-blocker assertions: no blacklisted seller eligible anywhere in the run; no off-domain checkout URL returned

tickets.title: Onboarding drives a shadow store to its first real bid
tickets.objective: An integration test walks the whole S6 seam in one run: a mocked interview transcript produces an economic envelope, the merchant approves it in writing, the store agent runs in shadow mode logging would-be bids without submitting any, and activation turns the same live intent into a real submitted bid. T-053 and T-043 each own one half of this seam and neither refs S6; this ticket asserts the join.
acceptance: 1. A mocked interview transcript yields an economic envelope carrying every R6 field: floors, max discount, budget cap, intents to pursue, and standing commitments.
2. Activation is refused while the envelope carries no recorded written merchant approval, and succeeds once it does (R6).

3. Before activation the store agent is in shadow mode: for a live intent it logs a would-be bid WITH its reasoning, and the exchange receives nothing — asserted by the absence of any bid_placed LedgerEvent for that auction, not merely by an empty return value (R7).
4. After activation the same live intent produces a real submitted bid, and a bid_placed LedgerEvent appears for it — so the test fails if activation is a no-op in either direction.
non_goals: The manual demo run on a fresh dev store — that is T-085's runbook.
New product code: this ticket asserts the join between T-053's onboarding and T-043's shadow mode; a gap it finds is a defect report against those tickets, not a fix here.
